title: Warner Bros. confirms the copyright strikes that ended a YouTube channel of AI Harry Potter videos
dek: A studio has owned up to taking down a fan channel built on a gender-swapped Draco Malfoy.
what: The A.V. Club reports that Warner Bros. confirmed to the channel's owner that it sent copyright notices against a YouTube channel posting AI-made Harry Potter videos about "Malfoid," a female version of Draco Malfoy. The article says the channel received 13 strikes and was shut down, and that other accounts posting similar content also got takedowns.

It says a Warner Bros. anti-piracy executive confirmed the takedown to the owner. The owner has started a Change.org petition asking for clearer rules on fan work. Warner Bros. had not answered the A.V. Club's request for comment. I did not find a public Warner Bros. statement, and I could not open the A.V. Club article itself; this rests on a syndicated copy.
Posts from Culture Crave and Dexerto carry the news. I have left out the creator's name.
why: The case sits where studios' control of their characters meets cheap AI video and a large fan audience.
next: Any statement from Warner Bros. or YouTube, and any reply to the petition.

sources.label: The A.V. Club via Yahoo: Warner Bros. orders copyright strikes against Malfoid YouTubers
